scope: Move every media reference off www.lawyard.org into a lawyard-owned origin, generate derivatives on write, and make the WordPress uploads directory a 12-month redirect tail instead of a dependency.
not_in_scope: Deciding whether www.lawyard.org cuts over to this app (separate decision, unblocked by this plan)
Video transcoding / Lawyard TV platform choice
Postgres data migration (already imported: 11,590 articles, 11,306 published)
decisions_proposed: One media origin owned by Lawyard: media.lawyard.org
Derivatives generated on write (hero-1600 / card-800 / thumb-400, WebP + AVIF), not on read
Content-addressed immutable filenames so cache headers can be 1 year
Public read via CDN, service-role write only
Origin: Cloudflare R2 preferred (zero egress); Supabase Storage acceptable if one-vendor simplicity outweighs egress cost
assumptions: WordPress uploads directory is a few GB and 9-15k files; measure before choosing a plan, do not assume
Traffic is unknown, so price on egress risk rather than projected monthly GB
No image is legally required to stay on the Bluehost host; redirects cover external backlinks
One engineer executes; effort figures are engineer-hours unless stated
Tobi's cutover decision is pending, so this plan must be safe to run before that decision
definition_of_done: Zero rows in articles.featured_image, articles.content, ad_slots.image_url, profiles.avatar_url, lawyers/chambers galleries and intro videos point at www.lawyard.org
Every image is served from media.lawyard.org with 2-3 pre-generated sizes and a 1-year immutable cache
wp-content/uploads/** 301s to the matching new URL for 12 months
A restore drill has been performed once (media is not in Postgres backups)

title: Measure the source before choosing anything
why: Every cost and risk in this plan is a function of the real uploads footprint, which nobody has measured.
steps: On Bluehost: du -sh wp-content/uploads && find wp-content/uploads -type f | wc -l && find wp-content/uploads -type f -printf '%s %p\n' | sort -rn | head -20
Record the largest file, total bytes, file count and the extensions present
Write the numbers into docs/CUTOVER.md §1 so the plan stops being an estimate
acceptance: Total bytes, file count and top-20 largest files recorded in docs/CUTOVER.md

title: Inventory every media reference in the database, per column
why: The cutover SQL only ever counted featured_image. Inline body images, ad creatives, galleries and avatars are separate rewrites with different mechanics.
steps: Run the reference queries below against production (read-only)
Save the counts as the baseline for the M5 gates
verify_sql: select count(*) from articles where featured_image like 'https://www.lawyard.org%';
select count(*) from articles where content like '%wp-content/uploads%';
select count(*) from ad_slots where image_url like 'https://www.lawyard.org%';
select count(*) from profiles where avatar_url like 'https://www.lawyard.org%';
select count(*) from lawyers where gallery::text like '%lawyard.org%';
select count(*) from chambers where gallery::text like '%lawyard.org%';
select count(*) from courses where cover_image like 'https://www.lawyard.org%';
acceptance: A single table of counts committed to docs/CUTOVER.md §1
No column with a media reference is missing from the list

title: Decide the origin and record it
why: R2 versus Supabase Storage changes the cost model, the upload code and the CDN setup — decide once, in writing.
steps: Price both against the measured footprint: storage, egress at 3 traffic scenarios, and operational overhead
Default to Cloudflare R2 behind media.lawyard.org unless one-vendor simplicity is explicitly preferred
Record the decision and the rejected option in docs/OPERATIONS.md
acceptance: docs/OPERATIONS.md carries the decision, the rejected alternative and the trigger that would reverse it

title: Provision the origin and the custom domain
why: Serving media from a host you own is what makes the next cutover reversible; a provider URL in the database is a lock-in.
steps: Create the bucket/namespace (R2: media-layard; or Supabase: keep buckets but plan the move)
Bind media.lawyard.org with TLS and a public read policy
Set Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable on the origin
Confirm a HEAD request returns the cache header and an image content-type
acceptance: curl -I https://media.lawyard.org/<test>.webp returns 200 with immutable cache and image/webp

title: Fix the path convention before the first upload
why: Paths are the one thing that cannot be refactored later cheaply — every stored URL and every external embed bakes them in.
steps: Adopt: articles/<slug>/hero-1600.webp | card-800.webp | thumb-400.webp, articles/<slug>/inline-<sha1>.webp
Adopt: ads/<ad-id>/creative-<sha1>.webp, profiles/<user-id>/avatar-320.webp, firms/<firm-id>/gallery-<sha1>.webp
Document the convention in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (Storage section) and reference it from lib/images.ts
acceptance: Convention documented
First uploaded asset follows it
No UUID-only filenames in new writes

title: Replace the upload route with a real ingest pipeline
why: The current route accepts any file whose client-declared MIME starts with image/, caps at 500KB, and stores one original under a random UUID — no derivatives, no EXIF strip, no magic-byte check.
steps: Validate by magic bytes, not file.type; reject anything that is not jpeg/png/webp/avif
Raise the cap for originals (e.g. 10MB) but enforce derivative sizes at generation
Strip EXIF, convert to WebP (and AVIF where supported), generate hero/card/thumb
Hash the source and name derivatives by content hash; skip if already present (dedupe)
Return a manifest {key, width, height, variants[]} instead of a single url
acceptance: Uploading a 12MP jpeg yields 3 WebP derivatives under the documented path
A duplicate upload writes no new bytes
A renamed .exe fails the magic-byte check

title: Make the read helper derive srcsets instead of single URLs
why: Every component currently passes one URL to /; that is why cards download hero-sized files.
steps: Extend lib/images.ts with coverImage(value) -> {src, srcSet, sizes, width, height}
Keep coverUrl()/COVER_PLACEHOLDER as the fallback path for legacy or junk values
Support both remote R2 keys and already-absolute Supabase URLs during the transition
acceptance: One component renders a srcset with 3 candidates and an explicit width/height
Existing placeholder behaviour preserved for invalid values

title: Migrate the three ad creatives first
why: They are live revenue, they are the smallest set, and they break the moment WordPress stops answering.
steps: Download the three seeded images, run them through the M1.3 ingest, update ad_slots.image_url
Add an upload control to /admin/ads so no future creative is entered as a hotlink
Verify each slot renders from media.lawyard.org on the corporate post page
acceptance: select count(*) from ad_slots where image_url like 'https://www.lawyard.org%' = 0
Banners render with correct aspect ratio and no layout shift

title: Migrate the 9,586 article covers, idempotently
why: This is the bulk of the risk: half the corpus loses its image on the day the old host retires.
steps: Write scripts/migrate-media.mjs: select id, slug, featured_image where it matches the WP host, in pages of 100
Per row: download (retry with backoff), hash, generate derivatives, upload, update featured_image to media.lawyard.org
Skip any URL already present by hash; log every failure with its URL and HTTP status
Resume from a checkpoint file; never re-download a finished page
Run in dry-run mode first and diff the intended updates against a 20-row sample
acceptance: Zero WP-host covers remain
The run is resumable (kill it mid-way, restart, no duplicate uploads)
Failures are itemised, not swallowed
verify_sql: select count(*) from articles where featured_image like 'https://www.lawyard.org%'; -- must reach 0

title: Migrate inline body images
why: Covers are the visible half; around 400 bodies carry pointing at the old host, and those are invisible until an article is read.
steps: Extract distinct wp-content URLs from articles.content
Ingest each once, then rewrite the HTML through the existing sanitiser pass
Re-sanitise after rewriting so no attribute is introduced outside the allowlist
acceptance: select count(*) from articles where content like '%wp-content/uploads%' = 0
A sampled article renders all body images from the new origin

title: Migrate profile, firm and listing assets
why: Avatars, firm galleries and intro videos are the same class of dependency and are currently split across three buckets.
steps: Migrate avatars, firm galleries, listing photos and course covers using the same script
Leave intro videos in Supabase Storage unless they exceed ~50MB, in which case route them to the video decision (out of scope)
Normalise the stored value for each column to the documented key/URL shape
acceptance: No media column contains a WP host
Each column's expected shape is documented next to the migration

title: Allow the new host in next/image and switch components to the helper
why: next/image rejects unknown hosts at build; and until components stop passing raw URLs, derivatives never get used.
steps: Add media.lawyard.org to next.config.js remotePatterns; keep the WP host allowed until M5.1 passes
Switch ArticleCard, the corporate post page, admin thumbnails and profile surfaces to coverImage()/srcset
Remove the per-component eslint-disable no-img-element only where <Image> is genuinely used
acceptance: pnpm build succeeds
Cards request card-sized files (check network tab, not just markup)

title: Decide image optimisation: pre-generated sizes or Next's optimiser
why: Running both is the classic double-transform cost — pre-generated derivatives plus on-demand optimisation of the same asset.
steps: Default: serve pre-generated derivatives directly (unoptimized) and skip the Vercel optimiser
If <Image> optimisation is kept, whitelist only the new host and watch the optimiser quota for a week
Record the choice and its cost signal in docs/OPERATIONS.md
acceptance: One transform path in production
A page loads at most 3 image variants

title: 301 the old uploads paths for 12 months
why: External backlinks, WhatsApp/LinkedIn embeds and image search point at wp-content URLs and will not re-crawl on your schedule.
steps: Map wp-content/uploads/<path> to the migrated asset where the filename is unique
For unmapped files, redirect to the nearest article or to a neutral placeholder — never 404
Implement as a redirect rule at the edge (Vercel/Cloudflare) and keep WordPress answering until it is live
Set a calendar reminder for removal at +12 months
acceptance: 20 sampled legacy image URLs return 301 to a live asset
No legacy image URL in the sample returns 404

title: Archive originals once, then stop paying for them
why: You need the originals for re-derivatives (better codec, new sizes) but not publicly served.
steps: Export the uploads directory to cold storage with a manifest (path, size, sha1)
Confirm the manifest matches the migrated derivative set before deleting anything from the public host
Record the archive location and restore command in docs/OPERATIONS.md
acceptance: Manifest file exists with one row per original
A random original can be restored and re-derived from the archive

title: Run the zero-reference gate across every column
why: A green gate is the only acceptable evidence that the dependency is gone; per-page spot checks hide whole columns.
steps: Re-run the M0.2 query set
Require zero rows for every query
Attach the output to docs/CUTOVER.md §7
acceptance: All counts are 0 and pasted into the cutover checklist

title: Crawl a 200-URL sample and assert no broken media
why: Database counts prove references moved; only a crawl proves bytes resolve, including og:image and in-body images.
steps: Crawl 200 URLs drawn from sitemap.ts across article types
Assert every image response is 200 and content-type is an image
Check og:image resolves absolutely (social previews break silently otherwise)
acceptance: Zero non-200 image responses in the sample
og:image validates in a social preview debugger for 3 sampled articles

title: Update the cutover gate so the blocker cannot silently return
why: New content written by the old pipeline could reintroduce a WP-host URL the day after the gate passes.
steps: Keep the SQL assertions in docs/CUTOVER.md §7
Add a CI or scheduled check that fails when any media column references the WP host
acceptance: A run fails loudly when a WP-host URL is inserted

title: Give media its own durability plan
why: Postgres point-in-time recovery does not restore files; today media has no restore story at all.
steps: Enable object versioning or a nightly export of the media namespace
Perform one restore drill into a scratch bucket
Document RPO/RTO in docs/OPERATIONS.md §2
acceptance: A deleted asset is recoverable in the drill
Restore steps written down

title: Monitor cost and orphans
why: Media egress is the only cost that grows with someone else's behaviour; orphans are the only storage that grows with nothing.
steps: Set a monthly egress/storage alarm at 2x the baseline
Add a monthly job that lists objects with no DB reference older than 30 days
Report both in the same place as the ad delivery numbers
acceptance: Alarm configured
Orphan report runs and is reviewed once

title: Codify the upload rules so the problem cannot come back
why: The dependency was created by pasting external URLs into a text field. Any field that accepts a URL will be used that way again.
steps: Every media-bearing admin field offers upload, not just a URL input
Reject non-owned hosts at write time (allow only media.lawyard.org and the legacy host during transition)
Document the rule in docs/OPERATIONS.md
acceptance: Pasting a WP-host URL into an admin form is refused with a clear message

title: Close the loop in the docs and the decision log
why: The repository is the handover artefact; an unrecorded decision is a decision the next session will re-litigate.
steps: Unblock docs/CUTOVER.md §1 (media) and note what remains
Record origin choice, path convention, derivative policy and cost model in docs/OPERATIONS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
Log the session in docs/data/timeline.json with the measured before/after counts
acceptance: pnpm docs:check passes
CUTOVER §1 is no longer a blocker and says so explicitly
